notes.front: What is security information and event management (SIEM)?
notes.back: A system that collects security data from across an organisation’s whole environment, on-premises and cloud, and analyses it to surface threats.
notes.explanation: It turns scattered logs and events into alerts and incidents that analysts can act on.
notes.example: Like a building’s central control room, where every camera and door sensor feeds one set of screens.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “What is SIEM?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is security orchestration, automation, and response (SOAR)?
notes.back: A system that takes alerts from a SIEM and other security tools and triggers automated workflows to handle the response.
notes.explanation: It takes the SIEM’s alerting a step further, from noticing a threat to acting on it.
notes.example: Like a fire system that not only sounds the alarm but also closes the fire doors and calls the brigade.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “What is SOAR?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In security operations, what is an incident?
notes.back: A case file that groups related alerts into one potential threat, for further investigation.
notes.explanation: Grouping means analysts review one threat with its context instead of many separate alerts.
notes.example: Like a police case folder that gathers several witness reports about the same break-in.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “What is SIEM?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In security monitoring, what is a false positive?
notes.back: An alert that turns out not to represent a real threat.
notes.explanation: Many alerts are of this kind, and each one still costs an analyst time to review.
notes.example: Like a smoke alarm set off by burnt toast.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “The role of AI and machine learning in modern SIEM/SOAR”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is alert fatigue?
notes.back: The state of analysts overwhelmed by the volume of alerts, who may start dismissing them without a proper review.
notes.explanation: Dismissing alerts unchecked creates exactly the gap an attacker can exploit.
notes.example: Like a car alarm that goes off so often that nobody on the street looks up any more.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “Alert fatigue and the importance of context”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Microsoft Sentinel?
notes.back: Microsoft’s scalable, cloud-native SIEM and SOAR solution, for detecting, investigating, hunting and responding to threats.
notes.explanation: It brings AI-powered analytics and threat intelligence across multicloud and multiplatform environments into one solution.
notes.example: Like one security company that runs both the monitoring room and the response team.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is the Microsoft Sentinel data lake?
notes.back: Sentinel’s cost-effective, long-term storage tier for security data, holding a mirrored single copy in an open format.
notes.explanation: It sits beside the analytics tier, where data first lands and analytics rules run.
notes.example: Like an archive warehouse behind a busy shop: the shelves hold what is needed today, the warehouse keeps years of stock cheaply.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Microsoft Sentinel data lake”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is the Microsoft Sentinel graph?
notes.back: A Sentinel component that models relationships between assets, identities, activities and threat intelligence.
notes.explanation: Teams reason over connected data to see how a threat moves, instead of searching isolated tables.
notes.example: Like a map of who knows whom in an organisation, rather than a list of names.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Microsoft Sentinel graph”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is the Microsoft Sentinel MCP server?
notes.back: A hosted model context protocol interface that lets people and AI agents work with Sentinel data in natural language.
notes.explanation: Users need no knowledge of the data schema and no custom code.
notes.example: Like an interpreter at a desk: you ask in plain words and they fetch the answer from the records.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Microsoft Sentinel MCP server”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Microsoft Sentinel, what is an analytics rule?
notes.back: A rule that regularly queries collected data and raises alerts when it finds suspicious activity.
notes.explanation: Sentinel then groups related alerts into incidents for the team to assign and investigate.
notes.example: Like a night guard who checks the same list of doors every hour and radios in if one is open.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Threat detection capabilities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Microsoft Sentinel, what is the content hub?
notes.back: The central place to discover and deploy packaged solutions, each bundling several content types for an end-to-end scenario.
notes.explanation: It also offers prebuilt rule templates, so teams need not write detection logic from scratch.
notes.example: Like an app store where each download is a complete kit rather than a single tool.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Threat detection capabilities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is threat hunting in Microsoft Sentinel?
notes.back: Proactively running hunting queries across your data to find suspicious activity that has not yet triggered a rule.
notes.explanation: The team does not wait for an alert; it goes looking.
notes.example: Like a doctor’s screening test, looking for disease before any symptom appears.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Threat investigation and hunting”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Microsoft Sentinel, what is an automation rule?
notes.back: A rule for centrally managing how incidents are handled: you set conditions and the actions to take when they are met.
notes.explanation: Its actions include assigning the incident, adding tasks, changing status or triggering a playbook.
notes.example: Like a post room rule: every parcel marked “urgent” goes straight to the manager’s desk.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Threat response and mitigation”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In SOAR and in Microsoft Sentinel, what is a playbook?
notes.back: A predefined sequence of automated actions run in response to an alert or incident. Sentinel builds them on Azure Logic Apps.
notes.explanation: The steps run without a person starting each one, which shortens the time from detection to containment.
notes.example: Like a restaurant’s closing checklist that runs itself: lights off, alarm set, manager texted.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Threat response and mitigation”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Microsoft Security Copilot?
notes.back: Microsoft’s AI assistant for security teams; with Sentinel it summarises incidents, suggests responses and turns plain-language requests into hunting queries.
notes.explanation: It surfaces context and suggestions faster; it does not replace the analyst’s judgement.
notes.example: Like a well-read research assistant who drafts the briefing, while you still make the call.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Sentinel integration with Microsoft Security Copilot, “Describe Microsoft Sentinel integration with Microsoft Security Copilot”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which SIEM function consolidates logs and security events from firewalls, servers, identity systems and devices into one platform?
notes.back: Log aggregation.
notes.explanation: Once the data is gathered, the SIEM analyses it to surface potential threats.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “What is SIEM?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which SIEM function looks for patterns and relationships between events, so that harmless-looking events together reveal a threat?
notes.back: Correlation.
notes.explanation: An event that seems innocent alone can matter when combined with others.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “What is SIEM?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which SIEM function produces notifications of suspicious activity for analysts to review?
notes.back: Alerting.
notes.explanation: Analysts then decide whether a genuine threat is present.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “What is SIEM?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which SIEM function automatically groups related alerts into case files?
notes.back: Incident creation.
notes.explanation: Those case files, incidents, represent one potential threat for further investigation.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “What is SIEM?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which SIEM function gives analysts one view of security activity across the whole organisation?
notes.back: Centralised visibility.
notes.explanation: Analysts no longer have to check each system separately.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “What is SIEM?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: According to the SIEM training unit, how does detection time compare without and with a SIEM?
notes.back: Without one, a breach can take days or weeks to detect; with one, detection can come within minutes.
notes.explanation: Faster detection is critical for limiting an attack’s impact.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “What is SIEM?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In SOAR, what does orchestration mean?
notes.back: Connecting different security tools and systems so they work together in a coordinated way.
notes.explanation: One detection can set several tools working at once, such as an identity lookup and a threat-intelligence check.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “What is SOAR?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In SOAR, what does automation mean?
notes.back: Carrying out repetitive, time-consuming response tasks without manual effort.
notes.explanation: The platform runs the same steps an analyst would otherwise repeat every time a given alert fires.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “What is SOAR?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: SIEM provides {{c1::visibility}}, while SOAR provides speed.
notes.back: Visibility.
notes.explanation: SIEM collects, correlates and surfaces threats; SOAR automates the response to them.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “Why SIEM and SOAR work better together”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are two benefits of a combined SIEM and SOAR solution?
notes.back: Any two of: one source of security data and context; faster automated response; consistent, repeatable processes; more analyst time for complex work.
notes.explanation: Without it, teams hop between disconnected tools, which slows response and risks missing signals.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “Why SIEM and SOAR work better together”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which AI capability in modern SIEM and SOAR learns a baseline of normal behaviour and flags departures from it?
notes.back: Anomaly detection.
notes.explanation: A user touching resources for the first time, for instance, stands out against the learned baseline.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “The role of AI and machine learning in modern SIEM/SOAR”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which AI capability in modern SIEM and SOAR groups related alerts into incidents and judges their severity?
notes.back: Alert correlation and prioritisation.
notes.explanation: It lets analysts deal with the highest-priority threats first.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “The role of AI and machine learning in modern SIEM/SOAR”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which AI capability in modern SIEM and SOAR uses models trained on history to tell genuine threats from benign activity?
notes.back: False positive reduction.
notes.explanation: Fewer false alarms means fewer alerts for analysts to review.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “The role of AI and machine learning in modern SIEM/SOAR”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which AI capability in modern SIEM and SOAR links low-level signals spread over days or weeks into one attack pattern?
notes.back: Multi-stage attack detection.
notes.explanation: Each step may look benign alone and not trigger an alert by itself.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “The role of AI and machine learning in modern SIEM/SOAR”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which AI capability in modern SIEM and SOAR helps analysts write queries and summarise incidents by asking in plain language?
notes.back: Natural language assistance.
notes.explanation: It lowers the technical bar for effective analysis.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “The role of AI and machine learning in modern SIEM/SOAR”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does incident grouping reduce alert fatigue?
notes.back: It merges related alerts from different sources into one incident with all the context attached.
notes.explanation: The analyst reviews one well-formed incident instead of dozens of alerts about the same attack.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “Alert fatigue and the importance of context”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which severity levels does the SIEM training give as examples for alerts and incidents?
notes.back: Informational, low, medium and high.
notes.explanation: Severity reflects potential impact and how likely the threat is to be genuine.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “Alert fatigue and the importance of context”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does automatic enrichment add to an alert, to fight alert fatigue? Give two examples.
notes.back: Any two of: known threat intelligence, user account history, device compliance status, location data.
notes.explanation: Analysts get the context to decide quickly without gathering it from several systems.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “Alert fatigue and the importance of context”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: From where does Microsoft Sentinel collect and correlate signals?
notes.back: From all users, devices, applications and infrastructure, whether on-premises, in Azure or in other clouds.
notes.explanation: That breadth gives the security team one view of threats across the enterprise.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Microsoft Sentinel as a SIEM”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Sentinel’s four areas of security operations, what happens in the “collect” area?
notes.back: Security data is gathered at cloud scale through data connectors, and normalised into a uniform view.
notes.explanation: Normalising different formats makes events from separate sources easier to correlate.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Microsoft Sentinel as a SIEM”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Sentinel’s four areas of security operations, what happens in the “detect” area?
notes.back: Analytics rules and AI-powered detections find threats, reduce false positives and group alerts into incidents.
notes.explanation: Rules run regularly against collected data and raise alerts on suspicious activity.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Microsoft Sentinel as a SIEM”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Sentinel’s four areas of security operations, what happens in the “investigate” area?
notes.back: AI-assisted tools and proactive hunting reveal an attack’s full scope and root cause.
notes.explanation: This is where the team works out what really happened.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Microsoft Sentinel as a SIEM”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Sentinel’s four areas of security operations, what happens in the “respond” area?
notes.back: Built-in orchestration and automation limit a threat’s impact without manual intervention.
notes.explanation: This is Sentinel acting in its SOAR role.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Microsoft Sentinel as a SIEM”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Microsoft Sentinel offers {{c1::more than 350}} built-in data connectors, for Microsoft services, non-Microsoft platforms and custom sources.
notes.back: More than 350.
notes.explanation: The connectors are how Sentinel gathers data from across the digital estate.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Microsoft Sentinel as a SIEM”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: The Azure portal experience for Microsoft Sentinel retires on {{c1::31 March 2027}}; after that, Sentinel is available only in the Microsoft Defender portal.
notes.back: 31 March 2027.
notes.explanation: The Defender portal is already the recommended place to use Sentinel.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Microsoft Sentinel as a SIEM”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Microsoft Sentinel, what is the analytics tier, and what runs there?
notes.back: A Log Analytics workspace where data lands first; real-time alerting, hunting, incident management and analytics rules run there.
notes.explanation: Data from it is mirrored to the data lake tier for long-term storage.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Microsoft Sentinel data lake”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: The Microsoft Sentinel data lake tier can keep security data for up to {{c1::12 years}}.
notes.back: 12 years.
notes.explanation: Long retention supports investigating persistent threats and building behaviour baselines from months of history.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Microsoft Sentinel data lake”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Sentinel detection approach matches data against known threat signatures and defined conditions?
notes.back: Rule-based detection.
notes.explanation: Prebuilt rule templates from Microsoft security experts are available through the content hub.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Threat detection capabilities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Sentinel detection approach learns behaviour baselines and flags unusual deviations?
notes.back: AI and machine learning detection.
notes.explanation: It can catch advanced attacks that individual rules would miss.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Threat detection capabilities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Sentinel’s correlation engine that links low-severity signals from many sources into high-confidence incidents is called {{c1::Fusion}}.
notes.back: Fusion.
notes.explanation: It helps surface multistage attacks that single rules might miss.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Threat detection capabilities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Sentinel detection approach checks ingested data against indicators of known malicious addresses and domains?
notes.back: Threat intelligence matching.
notes.explanation: Matches reveal activity tied to known threat actors.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Threat detection capabilities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are two content types a content hub solution can bundle?
notes.back: Any two of: data connectors, workbooks, analytics rules, hunting queries, playbooks.
notes.explanation: Bundling them lets one deployment cover a complete scenario.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Threat detection capabilities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does a Microsoft Sentinel incident bring together? Name two.
notes.back: Any two of: alerts, affected entities, timelines, context.
notes.explanation: All the evidence sits in one place for the team to assign, triage and investigate.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Threat investigation and hunting”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Sentinel, what can you do with a hunting query that finds something significant?
notes.back: Promote it into a custom analytics rule, so it raises alerts automatically from then on.
notes.explanation: A one-off search becomes ongoing detection.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Threat investigation and hunting”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are two conditions an automation rule in Sentinel can test?
notes.back: Any two of: incident severity, source, entity type.
notes.explanation: When the conditions match, the rule takes its actions on the incident.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Threat response and mitigation”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Microsoft Sentinel playbooks are automated workflows built on {{c1::Azure Logic Apps}}.
notes.back: Azure Logic Apps.
notes.explanation: They carry out a sequence of remediation actions when an automation rule triggers them.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Threat response and mitigation”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In which two experiences does Security Copilot work with Microsoft Sentinel?
notes.back: Embedded in the Microsoft Defender portal, and in the standalone Security Copilot experience through plugins.
notes.explanation: Standalone, it connects to Sentinel as a data source for chat-style questions.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Sentinel integration with Microsoft Security Copilot, “How the integration works”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does Security Copilot generate automatically when an analyst opens a Sentinel incident?
notes.back: A natural-language summary of what happened, the entities involved and the likely impact.
notes.explanation: It spares the analyst from reviewing every alert and log entry by hand.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Sentinel integration with Microsoft Security Copilot, “Incident summarization”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Are Security Copilot’s guided responses automated actions?
notes.back: No. They are suggestions, grouped as triage, containment, investigation and remediation, that help analysts decide.
notes.explanation: They are especially useful to less experienced team members.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Sentinel integration with Microsoft Security Copilot, “Guided responses”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Security Copilot capability turns a plain-language description into a ready-to-run hunting query?
notes.back: Natural language to KQL.
notes.explanation: Analysts who are not experts in Kusto Query Language can take part in hunting.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Sentinel integration with Microsoft Security Copilot, “Natural language to KQL for threat hunting”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Security Copilot agent classifies alerts at scale, saying which are real attacks and which are false positives?
notes.back: The Security Alert Triage Agent.
notes.explanation: It shows step-by-step reasoning for each verdict, so analysts can focus on genuine threats.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Sentinel integration with Microsoft Security Copilot, “AI agents”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A hospital’s analysts check firewall, server and identity logs in five separate consoles. They want one place that gathers and analyses them all. What kind of system do they need?
notes.back: A: A SIEM.
notes.choices:
A) A SIEM
B) A web application firewall
C) A hardware security module
D) A network security group
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: a web application firewall filters web traffic; it does not gather logs. C is wrong: a hardware security module protects keys. D is wrong: a network security group filters network traffic.
notes.explanation: A SIEM aggregates logs from many sources and analyses them in one platform.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “What is SIEM?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A late-night sign-in looks harmless, but the same account then downloads thousands of files. Which SIEM function connects these into a threat?
notes.back: D: Correlation.
notes.choices:
A) Centralised visibility
B) Alert fatigue
C) Log aggregation
D) Correlation
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: visibility shows everything in one view but does not link events. B is wrong: alert fatigue is a problem, not a function. C is wrong: aggregation gathers the logs.
notes.explanation: Correlation looks for relationships that make separate events significant together.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “What is SIEM?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Every phishing alert makes an analyst do the same five manual steps. The firm wants these to run by themselves when the alert fires. What should it add?
notes.back: B: SOAR with a playbook.
notes.choices:
A) A SIEM
B) SOAR with a playbook
C) Security defaults
D) A Microsoft Sentinel data lake
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: a SIEM detects and alerts but does not run response workflows. C is wrong: security defaults set identity protections. D is wrong: the data lake stores data long term.
notes.explanation: SOAR playbooks run predefined steps automatically when an alert fires.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “What is SOAR?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Analysts receiving thousands of alerts a day have started closing them unread. What is this, and what helps?
notes.back: C: Alert fatigue; group related alerts into incidents.
notes.choices:
A) Data poisoning; retrain the model
B) A false positive; delete the rule
C) Alert fatigue; group related alerts into incidents
D) Lateral movement; isolate the device
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: data poisoning corrupts a model’s data. B is wrong: one false alarm is not the pattern described, and deleting rules loses coverage. D is wrong: lateral movement is an attacker’s technique, not a state analysts fall into.
notes.explanation: Incident grouping, severity scoring and enrichment are how platforms counter alert fatigue.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “Alert fatigue and the importance of context”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Twelve alerts about the same compromised mailbox arrive from three tools. What should the analyst ideally work from?
notes.back: D: One incident grouping the related alerts with their context.
notes.choices:
A) Twelve separate alerts, one by one
B) A new analytics rule
C) The secure score
D) One incident grouping the related alerts with their context
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: that is the pattern that leads to fatigue. B is wrong: a new rule would add more alerts. C is wrong: secure score measures posture.
notes.explanation: An incident is the case file that gathers related alerts about one threat.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “What is SIEM?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A manufacturer wants one Microsoft cloud-native service that is both its SIEM and its SOAR, across Azure and Amazon Web Services. What should it choose?
notes.back: B: Microsoft Sentinel.
notes.choices:
A) Microsoft Defender for Cloud
B) Microsoft Sentinel
C) Azure Monitor alerts
D) Microsoft Purview
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: Defender for Cloud manages posture and workload protection, not SIEM. C is wrong: they notify on monitoring data; the training names Sentinel as Microsoft’s SIEM and SOAR. D is wrong: Purview handles data governance and compliance.
notes.explanation: Sentinel is Microsoft’s cloud-native SIEM and SOAR across multicloud environments.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A Sentinel team is working out an attack’s root cause and how far it spread. Which of Sentinel’s four areas are they in?
notes.back: D: Investigate.
notes.choices:
A) Collect
B) Detect
C) Respond
D) Investigate
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: collect is gathering data. B is wrong: detect finds the threat in the first place. C is wrong: respond limits the impact.
notes.explanation: Investigation establishes an attack’s full scope and root cause.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Microsoft Sentinel as a SIEM”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A firm wants Sentinel to ingest logs from a non-Microsoft firewall without writing its own integration. What should it look for first?
notes.back: B: One of Sentinel’s built-in data connectors.
notes.choices:
A) A playbook
B) One of Sentinel’s built-in data connectors
C) An automation rule
D) The Microsoft Sentinel graph

notes.front: How does SIEM differ from SOAR?
notes.back: SIEM collects and correlates data to surface threats; SOAR orchestrates and automates the response to them.
notes.explanation: They are complementary: one brings visibility, the other speed.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “Why SIEM and SOAR work better together”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Is disabling a flagged account automatically, without an analyst starting it, a SIEM or a SOAR task?
notes.back: SOAR: it is an automated response action.
notes.explanation: SIEM’s part ends at detection and alerting; SOAR runs the response steps.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “What is SOAR?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does orchestration differ from automation in SOAR?
notes.back: Orchestration makes separate tools work together; automation performs repetitive tasks without a person.
notes.explanation: One is about coordination across systems, the other about removing manual effort.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “What is SOAR?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: When an alert fires, a SOAR platform queries the identity system, checks a threat-intelligence feed and messages the team, all coordinated together. Is making those tools work together orchestration or automation?
notes.back: Orchestration: it connects separate tools so they act in concert.
notes.explanation: Automation is the removal of manual effort from repeated steps; orchestration is the coordination across systems.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Define the concepts of SIEM and SOAR, “What is SOAR?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does an automation rule differ from a playbook in Microsoft Sentinel?
notes.back: An automation rule centrally decides how incidents are handled; a playbook is a Logic Apps workflow of remediation steps, which a rule can trigger.
notes.explanation: Rule actions include assigning an incident or changing its status; a playbook runs a sequence of remediation actions.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Threat response and mitigation”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does threat hunting differ from an analytics rule in Sentinel?
notes.back: Hunting is a person searching proactively for what no rule has caught; an analytics rule runs regularly and raises alerts automatically.
notes.explanation: A useful hunting query can be promoted into a rule.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel, “Threat investigation and hunting”
